category: Taxi fare far above route baseline
signals: Fixed fare quote above route baseline
Quoted fare is about 8x above route baseline (800 THB vs ~100 THB local reference)
Pickup pressure to pay upfront before getting in
next_steps: Decline this ride and walk back into the BTS station or a hotel lobby; do not get into a taxi that refuses the meter.
Use Grab, Bolt, or your hotel's official taxi desk; the Siam to Wat Pho route should be about 60-120 THB on the meter (about 8 km, 15-25 minutes off-peak).
Save a photo of the taxi plate, the pickup point, the time, and the quoted fare in case you want to file a complaint.
If a driver follows you, blocks your path, or pressures you to get in, walk to the BTS staff or hotel front desk and ask them to help.
Optional: file a Bangkok taxi complaint via the Department of Land Transport hotline 1584 or via JS100 radio at 1137.
why_it_matters: 800 THB is about 8x the upper end of the local route baseline (about 60-120 THB metered for Siam to Wat Pho, ~8 km). A 'meter is broken' claim combined with a fixed-fare quote that high is the most common tourist-targeted overcharging script in central Bangkok. Bangkok law requires metered fares for green-yellow taxis (first km 35 THB, then 6.50 THB/km from km 1-10, plus a small waiting-time charge in heavy traffic). A driver who refuses the meter is in violation of the Public Land Transport Act and should be declined.
thai_phrase: กรุณาเปิดมิเตอร์ครับ/ค่ะ ไม่งั้นขอเปลี่ยนคันได้ไหมครับ/ค่ะ
evidence_to_save: Photo of the taxi plate and the driver's posted ID card if visible
Pickup point (Siam BTS exit X) and intended destination (Wat Pho)
Time of the quote and any verbal threat or pressure
Quoted fare (800 THB) and how the driver explained it
Receipt or Grab/Bolt screenshot of the same-route reference fare if you choose another ride
contact_recommendation: No police escalation is needed for the fare alone — just decline the ride and use another option. If the driver follows you, blocks you, or threatens you, walk to BTS staff or a hotel front desk and have them contact Tourist Police 1155. You can also report the taxi to the Department of Land Transport hotline 1584 (English available) or the JS100 traffic radio line 1137.
